fields.quoted_span:
A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of 
a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 
2A:42-10.10).
fields.note: The four protected activities, the notice-first condition for complaints, and the right to sue for damages all match the Reprisal section. The 'organizes or joins' wording is a fair paraphrase of 'organizer, or member, of any lawful organization'.
The record has no key value, and the reprisal section states no numeric value.
The record has no effective date, and the guide gives none for this provision.

fields.quoted_span:
The law against reprisal applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, 
including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
fields.note: The summary, the owner-occupied exemption and the max-units value of 3 all match the text.

The guide cites N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10 for the reprisal provision. The 'et seq.' and 'Reprisal law' aliases are not in the text, but the section heading 'Reprisal - Civil Rights of Tenants' supports the second only loosely.
